Batch size and chunk width change GEMM shapes and potentially CUDA kernels, accumulation order, and rounding. Consequently, a standalone target dot product can differ from its score inside a candidate matrix; near-ties can reverse. TF32, autocast, and reduced-precision reductions add differences. Determinism repeats a fixed computation; it does not guarantee equality across shapes. [PyTorch numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html)

Recommended validation procedure: freeze features with `model.eval()` and inference mode; fix hardware/software, seeds, dtype, and precision settings; disable autocast and TF32 for an FP32 audit. Enable `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`, disable cuDNN benchmarking, and set `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` before CUDA initialization. For target consistency, use two passes: first extract each target score from its actual catalog chunk; then replay identical chunks and count competitors. Never substitute a separately computed target dot product. Sweep user-batch sizes, chunk widths, and partial final chunks, comparing scores and ranks. For strict chunk-size invariance, define a canonical scoring kernel with fixed per-dot reduction order; deterministic GEMM alone is insufficient. [PyTorch reproducibility](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/randomness.html), [cuBLAS reproducibility](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cublas/index.html#results-reproducibility)

Streaming rank validation needs only chunk scores and per-user counters: excluding the target, accumulate `g=count(score>target)` and `e=count(score==target)` over eligible candidates. The target’s possible one-based ranks are `[g+1,g+e+1]`; exact rank requires the evaluator’s tie rule. Alternatively, merge chunk-local top-k lists using one consistent total ordering. Validate against full candidate vectors for a small user subset, including exclusions and duplicate handling. `torch.topk` does not guarantee stable tied indices. Tolerance-based equality changes ranking semantics; FP64 recomputation diagnoses sensitivity but does not establish the original FP32 ranking. [PyTorch topk](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.topk.html)
